findings.finding: Ouster has beaten the TOP of its own revenue guide in each of the last two quarters (Q1 2026 ~$49m vs $45-48m guide; Q2 2026 $54.6m vs $49.5-52.5m guide, +9% vs the $50.0m consensus); the same overshoot on the Q3 guide of $54.5-57.5m implies ~$58-59.5m against a $56.2m consensus that sits at the guide midpoint, i.e. a +3-6% revenue beat.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 revenue beat of ~9% vs consensus was sold: -4.78% close-to-close (baseline) on a Q3 guide below the then $58.6m consensus (https://www.chartmill.com/news/OUST/Chartmill-53181-Ouster-NASDAQOUST-Drops-on-Soft-Q3-Guidance-Despite-Q2-Beat). Q1 2026 beat bought +2.78%. Beats have not been paid on their own.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus ($56.2m Zacks, $56.27m GuruFocus) sits exactly on the guide midpoint and Zacks reports the estimate unchanged for 60 days, i.e. the street has not built in the two-quarter habit of clearing the top. If the beat pattern were priced, consensus would sit at or above $57.5m. Counterweight already in the size: CEO said on the Q2 call there is 'not that much wiggle room' in the guide and that Rev8 ramp late in Q3 limits upside (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/08/13/ouster-oust-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/).
findings.independence: Q1 guide/actual from a different release: https://seekingalpha.com/pr/20501883 (Q1 2026 results, Q2 guide $49.5-52.5m) and https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1816581/000119312526085444/d78060dex991.htm (Q4 2025 release, Q1 guide $45-48m). Same company, different documents.

findings.finding: Q3 GAAP gross margin will step down roughly 10 points from Q2's 49%: Q2 included a $5.4m IEEPA tariff refund booked as a reduction of cost of sales (10-Q Note 2), which the CFO said is one-time; he guided normalized margin to 'high 30s' and called 35-40% 'the right range in the near term'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior Ouster print with a guided margin step-down of this size in the baseline; Q2's 49% GM print with the refund flagged was followed by -4.78% (driven by the revenue guide, not the margin).
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: Q3 consensus EPS of -$0.30 against Q2's -$0.27 is consistent with ~$5-6m less gross profit on flat revenue, which is what the normalization implies. The residual risk is headline: a GAAP GM printing 38-40% vs 49% reads as a 'margin collapse' to anyone not modelling the refund; and EPS sources disagree (-$0.08 TipRanks to -$0.30 Zacks), so some estimates may not have the step-down. The 10-Q also says $4.8m of IEEPA receivables plus interest was collected after June 30, which is cash, not a second P&L benefit.
findings.independence: CFO statement on the call, a different document: https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/08/13/ouster-oust-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/ ; call summary https://www.tipranks.com/news/company-announcements/ouster-inc-earnings-call-highlights-growth-momentum

findings.finding: The Q4 2026 guide is the swing: the company reaffirmed 'full-year revenue expectations unchanged' on the Q2 call against its 30-50% annual growth framework on $169m of 2025 revenue (=$220-254m); street FY2026 is $222m (31%, the bottom of that range), and with H1 at $103.6m and Q3 ~$56m the street's implied Q4 is ~$62m, while Rev8 was due to reach volume production by end-Q3 at a Benchmark line with >100k units/yr capacity.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guide-driven: Q2 2026 Q3 guide midpoint $56m vs $58.6m consensus -> -4.78%. Earlier guide/beat prints: +31.9% (2025-03-20), +22.8% (2025-05-08), +11.7% (2025-08-07) show the upside tail when guidance rises.
findings.why_not_priced: The stock has fallen 33% in 20 sessions and sits 46% below the July offering price, with skew paying for downside, which is what a priced Q4 disappointment looks like; yet the street's FY number already sits at the floor of the company's own reaffirmed framework, so an in-framework Q4 guide ($60-66m) is at or above the bar. What would be different if the market priced a Rev8-led Q4 step-up: FY consensus above the $222m floor and Q4 implied above $62m. Caveat in the size: the FY 30-50% target was stated as an annual framework, not a 2026 point guide, and the 2025 base includes ~$21m of one-time royalties, so the framework is a weaker bar than a range.
findings.independence: Q4 2025 release with the 30-50% framework and the $21m royalty: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1816581/000119312526085444/d78060dex991.htm ; Rev8 capacity: https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/oust-benchmark-manufacturing-deal-rev8-it-worth-hype ; FY consensus $222m: https://www.theglobeandmail.com/investing/markets/stocks/AEVA/pressreleases/8477980/ouster-q3-earnings-on-deck-buy-hold-or-sell-oust-stock-now/

findings.finding: Customer concentration is rising fast: one customer ('Customer E') was 32% of Q2 2026 revenue and 31% of H1 revenue, and 26% of receivables (another customer 30% of receivables), up from a reported 21% of 2025 revenue and 12% of 2024; one customer's order timing can move the quarter and the Q4 guide by several million dollars either way.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No print in the baseline where the concentration was named as the cause of a move.
findings.why_not_priced: It sits in a 10-Q note, not in any preview read here; no preview mentions it. Sign is genuinely two-sided, so sized near zero: the rest of the company (68% of revenue: industrial, smart infrastructure ~15% via BlueCity/Gemini, drones, Stereolabs) grew enough that total revenue rose 56% y/y in Q2, and a slowdown at Customer E would have to be large to break the guide.
findings.independence: 2025 concentration (21%, 12%->21%) from a secondary summary of the 10-K: https://www.panabee.com/news/ouster-earnings-2025-annual

findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Robotics/lidar names fell together on 2026-08-18 (Ouster -10%, Aeva -12%) on an AI selloff (https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/08/18/robotics-stocks-punished-tuesday-in-ai-sell-off-ouster-down-10-aeva-technologies-down-12-symbotic-down-4/); no post-print reaction measured from a sector-driven pre-print drawdown.
findings.why_not_priced: Weak by construction: absence of a filing is not a cause, and the put skew (+17 vol points) says the option market expects more downside. The one sourced cause is a proxy (a Korean report of a US AI-stock plunge on 2026-10-15, https://www.mt.co.kr/en/stock/2026/10/26/2026102611205496302 is the related late-October item).
